record_title: Bishop volume deficit controls curvature-operator excess
limitations: The theorem requires the strong pointwise lower bound R >= Id. It gives L1 control of curvature-operator magnitude but no higher-Lp estimate is established here without additional geometric input. The trace-norm coefficient and the even-dimensional nonlinear curvature-floor concentration law are sharp on round rescalings, while optimality is not claimed for each individual higher Lipschitz-Killing term. The odd-dimensional hierarchy is an inequality because of the nonnegative filling contribution. The result is a structural consequence of the very recent Ge-Li-Li curvature-integral theorem, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations remain a residual originality risk.
